title: Exploring the impact of perceived value on cultural communication willingness during visits to folklore museums: An analysis based on LDA and fsQCA
content:
by Yu Wen, Kexin Xu, Xiaoxia Li

The synergistic development of culture and tourism is an important driver of global economic growth. As key venues that bear collective memory and sustain cultural roots, folklore museums have assumed an increasingly prominent role in cultural communication and identity formation amid evolving social demands and a globalized context of national cultural identity. However, existing research has yet to fully elucidate the complex mechanisms by which perceived value in the folklore museum context shapes visitors’ willingness for cultural communication. Grounded in complexity theory, this study develops a configurational analysis framework linking perceived value, satisfaction, and cultural communication willingness. Using five Chinese folklore museums as cases, it combines Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), focusing on perceived content in visitors’ online reviews to identify five perceived value dimensions—cultural, functional, social, emotional, and conditional—and to reveal the intricate influence mechanisms through which these dimensions affect cultural communication willingness. From the perceived value configurational paths that yield high cultural communication willingness post-visit, the study identifies three perceived value–driven models: the Culture-Conditional-Functional Value Perception Driven Model, the Culture-Functional-Emotional Value Perception Driven Model, and the Culture-Social-Conditional Value Perception Driven Model, and proposes targeted enhancement strategies for each. Cultural value emerges as a core condition across all paths, functioning as an INUS condition—an indispensable yet not sufficient component within the pathways—underscoring its central driving role in perceived value combinations. The findings provide scientific guidance for optimizing and upgrading other cultural tourism destinations, while imparting sustained momentum to cultural heritage preservation and the enhancement of national soft power.
